question.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=\frac{3y-2x}{7y-6x}.$ The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ is given by

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{h(x,y)}{(7y-6x)^{2}}.
$$

Find the function $h(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{3y-2x}{7y-6x}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂x}(3y-2x)\cdot (7y-6x)-(3y-2x)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(7y-6x)}{(7y-6x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot (7y-6x)-(3y-2x)\cdot (-6)}{(7y-6x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-14y+12x+18y-12x}{(7y-6x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4y}{(7y-6x)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
h(x,y)=4y.
$$
